data.title: Apple Stock (AAPL) Ends Lower After Reports Surface of Weak iPhone 18 Demand
data.description:
Shares of Apple (AAPL) finished trading down nearly 2% on Oct. 9 following reports of weak demand for the company's new iPhone 18 smartphone. Media reports say that Apple is cutting production of its new iPhone 18 due to weak consumer demand globally. Apple has reportedly told suppliers to reduce production of components used in the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max models due to soft demand.

News of the weak demand and production cut come a month after Apple announced the newest versions of its iPhone, including its first foldable smartphone called the "Duo." Suppliers and analysts are blaming the company's price increases for the weak demand among consumers. Apple raised prices across its lineup of iPhones as it grapples with surging costs for memory chips and processors.
data.author: Joel Baglole

data.title: With Fortinet Stock at All-Time Highs, Here's What Can Move It Up or Down
data.description:
Cybersecurity company Fortinet (FTNT) could see stronger growth as more businesses look for ways to protect their networks and cloud applications through one security provider. To take advantage of this demand, Fortinet is expanding its SASE Firewall platform, which combines traditional firewall protection with cloud-based security. The strategy is already showing progress, with quarterly billings surpassing $2 billion after growing by 34% from the previous year. However, with the stock at all-time highs, we will take a look at both the catalysts and risks that can move the stock higher or lower.

Catalysts That Could Push Fortinet Stock Higher

Fortinet's growth opportunity comes from how businesses are changing the way they work. As more employees work remotely and companies rely more heavily on cloud applications, traditional firewalls are becoming less effective on their own. That creates an opportunity for Fortinet because its SASE Firewall platform combines network protection with cloud security services.

SASE stands for Secure Access Service Edge, which essentially means that businesses can protect employees and applications even when they are outside the company's main network. Fortinet took another step in this direction on July 28 when it introduced its FortiGate 1200G and FortiSASE Outpost products. These products allow businesses to use cloud-based security while keeping more control over where their security systems operate.

This could make Fortinet more attractive to businesses that want to simplify their security systems. Instead of purchasing separate products from multiple providers, companies can rely on Fortinet for more of their protection needs. Importantly, demand for these services is already growing. Fortinet's Unified SASE billings increased by 35% in the second quarter, while annual recurring revenue grew by 18% to $1.41 billion.

Separately, Fortinet received recognition from research firm Gartner (IT) in September 2026, when it was named a Leader in the Hybrid Mesh Firewall category. The company ranked highest for its ability to execute for the second consecutive year. That recognition could help Fortinet win more large customers because businesses often consider Gartner's evaluations when choosing cybersecurity providers.

Risks That Could Hold Fortinet Stock Back

One risk is that Fortinet's cloud security business might not grow fast enough to justify the stock's valuation. Competition is also an issue, especially as cybersecurity rival Palo Alto Networks (PANW) expands its own security platform. As more companies offer similar services, Fortinet could find it harder to attract new customers or charge higher prices. The stock's valuation makes these risks more important.

Based on the midpoint of its expected adjusted earnings of $3.41 to $3.47 per share, the stock trades at approximately 56 times its expected 2026 earnings. This means that investors are paying about $55 for every $1 of annual profit that Fortinet is expected to generate. At such a high valuation, even a small slowdown in growth could put pressure on the stock.

Another concern is that businesses may reduce their spending on new firewalls after recently upgrading their equipment. That would also affect Fortinet's subscription business because new firewall purchases often lead customers to buy additional security services.

Nevertheless, investors will get a better picture of the company's operations when it reports its third-quarter results on October 28.

Turning to Wall Street, analysts have a Hold consensus rating on FTNT stock based on seven Buys, 22 Holds, and three Buys assigned in the past three months, as indicated by the graphic below. data.title: Visa Stock (V) Closes at All-Time High. Here's What's Driving the Gains
data.description:
The stock of credit card giant Visa (V) finished trading at an all-time high on Oct. 9. Shares of Visa ended the day at $385.45, a record high. The stock has risen 7% in the past five trading sessions even as Treasury yields above 5% pressure the stocks of other financial institutions, notably commercial banks whose loans are expected to be impacted.

V stock is now up 12% over the last 12 months, due in large part to the gains over the past week. Driving the increase has been a series of news from the payments giant. Visa recently processed its first international card transactions in Syria, marking a significant milestone following the U.S. decision to remove Syria from its state sponsors of terrorism list.

Visa's AI and Crypto Moves

In another move, Visa partnered with Ant International to develop a new standard for payments processed through artificial intelligence (AI) agents, helping to create common standards to verify the agents. It was an example of how Visa is adapting to AI and using the technology to its advantage rather than letting it disrupt its business.

data.title: Canada's Economy Lost Nearly 70,000 Jobs in September, Erasing Gains on the Year: SHOP, LULU, QSR
data.description:
Canada's economy lost 68,300 jobs in September and the unemployment rate moved higher as U.S. tariffs continue to have an impact. The September job losses erased all of Canada's employment gains recorded earlier in the year. The September drop follows a decline of 41,700 jobs in August, according to Statistics Canada.

imports-shop-lulu-qsr">The unemployment rate in Canada during September rose to 6.5% from 6.4% in August. September was the first full month of employment data after a new round of U.S. tariffs took effect against Canada this summer. However, the largest job losses were in the public sector, particularly health care, social assistance and education, as the government cut international student permits.

The poor labor market report weighed on leading Canadian stocks such as Shopify (SHOP), Restaurant Brands International (QSR), and Lululemon Athletica (LULU).

Economists Views

Economists polled by Reuters had forecast an increase of 9,200 jobs and an unemployment rate of 6.5% in September. With September's decline, Canada has now lost a net 41,200 jobs this year, compared with a gain of 211,300 in the same period of 2025. Job losses were split almost evenly between full-time and part-time positions.

Manufacturing, a sector largely exposed to U.S. tariffs, lost a net 12,700 jobs in September. Economists have said the latest U.S. tariffs are unlikely to have a major impact on employment data in the coming months, but the September data suggests otherwise. The September job losses were also driven by an aging population leaving the workforce and slower immigration reducing the number of replacements.

Odds of Rate Hike in Canada

Financial markets are no longer pricing in a rate increase from the Bank of Canada later in October following the sizable job losses and weakening labor market. However, futures traders still see a marginal chance that Canada's central bank raises interest rates by 25 basis points in December of this year.

Employment among young people aged 15-24 fell by 48,000 positions in September after a smaller decline in August. Growth in average hourly wages for permanent employees accelerated to 2.3% year-over-year in September from 2% in August, said Statistics Canada. Canada's dollar weakened after the latest jobs report, falling 0.44% to 69.99 U.S. cents against the greenback.

data.title: 'Don't Get It Wrong,' Says Analyst as AST SpaceMobile Stock Takes a Beating
data.description:
AST SpaceMobile (NASDAQ:ASTS) stock is plunging nearly 12% on Friday after Elon Musk's SpaceX struck another deal that could strengthen its position in the satellite communications market. The Starlink operator has agreed to acquire nationwide 800 MHz spectrum licenses from Grain Management in a transaction valued at an estimated $8 billion, potentially expanding its ability to connect ordinary smartphones directly to satellites.

The development is particularly disappointing for AST, which had also pursued those frequencies but ultimately lost out to its larger rival. Adding to investor concerns, the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) recently approved SpaceX's plans for a 15,000-satellite second-generation constellation, giving Musk's company another opportunity to expand its wireless services.

However, while the selloff suggests investors are worried about AST's competitive prospects, Berenberg analyst Michael Filatov believes the market may be overlooking an important consequence of SpaceX's latest moves.

Promotion

High conviction ASTS bulls now have this Tradr ETF

Filatov argues that the implications extend well beyond the immediate loss of valuable spectrum, potentially creating opportunities that investors have yet to appreciate.

"We think that the decision by SpaceX to build its own network raises ASTS's strategic value," the analyst writes.

The reasoning comes down to how traditional wireless operators might respond to Musk's expansion plans. With Starlink preparing to compete directly for mobile subscribers, established telecom companies could become more interested in AST's partnership model, which allows them to offer satellite connectivity while retaining their customer relationships.

This possibility becomes particularly relevant when considering T-Mobile, which currently relies on Starlink to provide satellite-to-phone services. SpaceX's expansion into terrestrial wireless operations could eventually place the two companies in direct competition, despite their existing commercial relationship.

Filatov believes this development could open an unexpected door for AST, potentially bringing another prominent American wireless operator into its growing network of partners.

"We think that this raises the likelihood of a scenario in which T-Mobile sources D2D capability from ASTS through the joint venture or forms a direct partnership," the analyst explains.

Such an arrangement would give T-Mobile another satellite connectivity option while potentially providing AST with a valuable new customer. The recently formalized carrier joint venture could also offer an established framework for pursuing that relationship without requiring an entirely separate agreement.

Meanwhile, Filatov sees another reason investors shouldn't assume SpaceX has already secured a decisive technological advantage over AST. The newly acquired 800 MHz frequencies are not necessarily compatible with Starlink's current satellites, meaning their commercial benefits could take considerable time to materialize.

SpaceX expects to deploy its next-generation satellites through 2027, with 5G-quality connectivity now targeted for the first half of 2028. AST, by comparison, already operates low-band frequencies from orbit and aims to begin commercial services during 2027, potentially giving it an earlier opportunity to establish its capabilities.

Nevertheless, Filatov acknowledges that losing access to Grain's spectrum eliminates a potential catalyst previously highlighted by Filatov. Despite that disappointment, the analyst has left his financial forecasts unchanged, suggesting the setback does not undermine his expectations for AST's future performance.

To this end, Filatov assigns ASTS shares a Buy rating, while his $92 price target suggests shares will rebound about 82% from current levels. (To watch Filatov's track record, click here)

Wall Street also sees substantial recovery potential for AST SpaceMobile, with the average 12-month price target of $86.42 suggesting nearly 72% upside from current levels. However, analysts remain divided on whether the stock deserves a Buy rating, with 5 recommending purchases and 6 preferring to stay on the sidelines. That leaves ASTS with a Moderate Buy consensus. data.title: "A Bloodbath": Skydance (NYSE:SKYD) Stock Gains Despite Worries at the Sports Divisions
data.description:
It was just days ago when we found entertainment giant Skydance (SKYD) was planning to put a lot of emphasis on sports to improve its linear prospects. That honeymoon phase did not last long as a new report from Awful Announcing says that CBS Sports and TNT Sports are expected to produce "a bloodbath" of lost jobs. Investors took the report in stride and gave Skydance stock a nearly 2% boost in the closing minutes of Friday's trading. Skydance has seen a 45.41% loss in its share price over the past year.

Losing Sports Rights?

Just two days ago we found out that Skydance was going to be investing heavily in sports as a way to keep itself running as a linear project, which would then be used to fuel the digital side of things. Of course we also heard that Skydance was looking to land $6 billion in cost savings, and would likely be turning to some job cuts to do that. Exactly how many and where was unclear at the time, but a certain amount of redundancy and job loss was to be expected.

The sports rights that are likely to be cut are also likely to be the deals that TNT Sports landed after it lost access to the NBA. At the time, TNT Sports was looking for a wide range of unusual sports. A little over a year ago, in fact, we were comparing Warner's plan for sports to the fictional ESPN8, The Ocho. For Skydance to step in and say it doesn't want things like Extreme H Racing or the Supertri League does make a certain amount of sense.

No Renegotiation, Yet

Another unexpected wrinkle kicked in as a report from NBC Sports noted that, despite the growth of Skydance, there has been no attempt to renegotiate the deal between CBS and the National Football League (NFL). The current deal is set to expire after the 2029 season, but there has been no move made to change the terms of the deal.

Certainly the terms of the deal are likely to change once the contract expires. The NFL knows what it has and what it can likely get for those rights. The gains in Skydance's viewership will largely come in the streaming department, and this may only have a minimal impact on any deal between Skydance and the NFL.
